result.reasoning:
REFUTED. The reporter's arithmetic reproduces exactly, but only under a synthetic point mass ~6x larger than the real panel's, the behaviour they call a bug is the project's documented house convention, and both stated consequences are demonstrably false.

(1) The relative worst-two-tenths quota is the intended semantics, defined identically in three independent places. partura/steer.py:350 docstring for RewardContext.untradable says the screen is "frozen quote in the last 15 days among the worst fifth". scripts/sweep.py:67 builds the PRODUCTION benchmark screen as `cs_last_high20(neg(KNOWN), cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret), 15))` and scripts/sweep.py:116 the per-factor variant `seg_xfrozen_*` with the annotation "本因子,但剔掉近 15 日冻结盘口最重的 20%" — the identical key expression and the identical relative 20%. scripts/readable_report.py:35,42,45,70 and scripts/guidance_report.py:91 present it to the user as "把冻结盘口最重的两成排到最后". So `fr_rank > 0.8` at idea_search.py:100 matches the convention the sweep and the user-facing reports use; the suggested replacement `frozen > 0.9` would cut the trim from 20.03% to 6.50% of cells and make the GP reward's universe inconsistent with the screens everything downstream measures.

(2) The reproducible pathology needs >=38% of the cross-section at EXACTLY 1.0. My fine sweep (r1 [2]) locates the leak: locked names first survive at mass 38% (2.48% kept), 40% -> 51.72% kept with the per-day share jumping 0.00%/40.00% (sd 19.6%), >=45% -> nothing removed at all. The project's own real-data measurement of this very screen on this very window contradicts that mass: runs/*/anatomy_s*.json (45 files, split ['20180102','20230807']) all report the frozen-cell share as 6.4753%, and anatomy.py:109-112 measures it with the LOOSER `day_flat_ratio(Close) > 0.9` within 15 days, so the exactly-1.0 mass of `cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret), 15)` is <= 6.475%. At 6.5% the mask is a stable 20.016% +- 0.186% per day (min 19.650%, max 20.600%), removes 100% of the truly locked names, and is a strict SUPERSET of `frozen > 0.9` (0.0000% of locked cells missed). The claimed "blocks jumping between 0% and the whole block" and "52.5% of locked names left buyable" do not occur anywhere near the real mass.

(3) "候选之间的分数不可比" is false by construction. `ctx.untradable` is built once at idea_search.py:95-103 from `aux["frozen"]`, before the GP starts, and never depends on the candidate panel; every candidate therefore sees a byte-identical per-day universe (r1 [3]: five candidates, same per-day counts [1546, 1545, 1561, 1552, 1553], `same == True`). Any day-to-day universe variation is a common term across candidates, and the long_marginal baseline is re-ranked inside the same universe (RewardContext.pool_in_universe, partura/steer.py:366-375), so the difference is taken in one universe.

(4) "评估预算有两成固定花在一批被随机剔掉的正常股票上" is false. BUDGET (default 192) counts candidate EXPRESSIONS evaluated by run_mining, not stocks; the panel is computed over all names and the mask is applied inside the reward (`raw = np.where(ctx.untradable, np.nan, raw)`, partura/steer.py:421-422). Narrowing the universe consumes no budget.

(5) The "average rank vs ordinal rank means two different sets of stocks" claim also fails at the real mass. r4 compares the mask against the production operator `cs_last_high20` on the same key: at mass 6.5% the two sets agree on 99.50% of the mask / 99.72% of the operator's set (20.03% vs 19.99% of cells) — the same stocks up to boundary tie noise. Where they diverge (mass >= 25%) the OPERATOR is the worse behaved of the two: its ordinal tie-break demotes only the first 20% of the 1.0 block by column order, leaving 20.26% of truly locked names buyable, while the average-rank mask removes 100%.

Residual, unverified, and not the defect as reported: a crisis window (2020-02-03 plus the 15 days `cross_max` carries it, inside train) could in principle put a handful of days in the >=38% band, in which case those days' trim fires on nothing. I cannot test it (the minute store is remote and off-limits), and the 6.475% window average leaves room for at most ~16 such days. r3 bounds it: a 16-day failure out of 1370 shifts long_tradable scores by at most 0.23 against a discovery threshold of 1.0, and only reorders candidates already within ~0.26 of each other (i.e. statistically indistinguishable). Note too that `frozen >= 1.0` is not the primary tradability guard — the labels are `open_vwap15_buyable` and partura/panels.py:236-244 already NaNs out any name that opens locked at limit-up on the entry day.

Scripts: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/refute_untradable_quota/{r1_quota_vs_real_mass.py, r2_block_is_not_monolithic.py, r3_crisis_days_bound.py, r4_same_top20_as_production_screen.py}. No file outside that directory was touched.
result.reproduction: r1 [1] reproduces the report's own [A] verbatim: mass 0%/5%/15% -> untradable 20.02% (locked kept 0.00%), 25% -> 24.96%, 40% -> 19.00% with 52.46% of locked names kept. So the arithmetic is right. r1 [2] then sweeps the mass finely and anchors it to reality: the leak begins only at mass 38% (locked kept 2.48%), peaks at 40% (per-day share min 0.00% / max 40.00%, sd 19.595%, locked kept 51.72%) and reaches "removes nothing" at 45%; whereas at the mass the project itself measured on this window (6.475%, from 45 agreeing runs/*/anatomy_s*.json files) the per-day share is 20.016% +- 0.186% (min 19.650%, max 20.600%) with 0.00% of locked names kept. r1 [4]: at that mass the quota mask (20.02% of cells) is a strict superset of `frozen > 0.9` (6.50%) — 0.0000% of locked cells missed. r1 [3] scores five different candidate panels through partura.steer.reward(..., "long_tradable") against one RewardContext and gets identical per-day universes for all five (`same == True`), refuting the comparability claim. r2 checked whether a crisis block would split across values: it would not from minute-count variation (day_zero_ratio normalises by finite minutes, so 241/240/238/235 all-zero minutes all return exactly 1.000000), so the monolithic-block case is possible in principle — but it still requires >=38% at that single value. r4 shows the mask and the production `cs_last_high20` screen select the same stocks at the real mass (99.50%/99.72% agreement) and that the operator, not the mask, is the one that leaks at higher masses (mass 25%: operator removes 79.74% of locked names, mask 100.00%). r3 bounds the hypothetical crisis case at <=0.23 score shift versus a 1.0 threshold. Nothing I ran produced a wrong result from the code as written at any realistic input.
result.corrected_fix: Nothing needs fixing for the reported defect. Do NOT apply the suggested change: replacing the quota with `untradable_frozen = frozen > 0.9` drops the trim from 20.03% to 6.50% of cells and desynchronises the GP reward's universe from the `cs_last_high20(·, cross_max(day_zero_ratio(Ret), 15))` screens that scripts/sweep.py:67,116 evaluate and scripts/readable_report.py reports, i.e. it would change the selection criterion rather than correct it. If the unverified Feb-2020-style crisis window is worth hardening against, the correct form is additive and a no-op at the measured mass — add the absolute term as an OR, not a replacement, at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py:100: `untradable = (fr_rank > 0.8) | (frozen >= 1.0) | (age < 0.9 * possible) | ~np.isfinite(frozen)`. That keeps the worst-fifth convention intact (the quota already dominates whenever the mass is below 40%) and only bites on a day where the quota would otherwise fire on nothing, so it cannot move any existing number. The reporter's logging suggestion (write the per-day untradable share into evidence.json alongside the startup mean) is harmless and changes no number; the existing startup line already prints the whole-sample mean, which at 20% +- 0.19% would make any crisis-day collapse visible as a drop in that mean.
